## Abstract
The query asked whether GEO series GSE309890 provides raw reads and whether those reads can support an assembly workflow. I first retrieved the GEO Series record to determine study type, linked project identifiers, and supplementary files. I then resolved the linked BioProject (PRJNA1363958), queried NCBI links to SRA and BioSample, and listed all SRA runs for that project. Finally, I checked available reference assemblies and workflow compatibility in the BRC workflow resources. The GEO record reports 6 samples from *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, classified as “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing,” with 1 supplementary processed-expression file and no linked PubMed record. The linked BioProject contains 6 SRA runs, all public, all paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 RNA-Seq libraries, with per-run sizes of 801–955 MB and 10,415,434–11,992,461 spots. A complete reference genome assembly for the same strain is available as GCF_000005845.2. Compatible workflows include RNA-seq processing workflows, but no assembly workflow was retrieved for these short-read transcriptomic data. These results indicate that raw reads do exist, but they are transcriptomic RNA-seq reads rather than whole-genome DNA reads. Therefore, they are suitable for RNA-seq analysis against the MG1655 reference, not for a standard de novo genome assembly of the organism.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** GEO series GSE309890 is a gene expression study in *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The practical question is whether a GEO accession also exposes raw sequencing data and whether those data are suitable for assembly. This matters because GEO often stores processed expression outputs while raw reads may reside in SRA under a linked BioProject.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before querying the databases, it was unresolved whether GSE309890 had linked raw sequencing data and, if so, whether those data were genome-assembly appropriate.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine whether GSE309890 has retrievable raw reads and whether they can be used for assembly. The expectation was that GEO would link to SRA for raw data, but that an expression-profiling study would more likely provide RNA-seq reads than genome sequencing reads.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** I used GEO to identify the study and its linked project, NCBI BioProject/SRA to locate raw reads, and BRC organism/workflow resources to assess whether an assembly route was supported by the available organism and workflows.

**Materials.**  
- GEO via `functions.geo_series`  
- NCBI BioProject via `functions.ncbi_find_uids`  
- NCBI linked records via `functions.ncbi_linked_records`  
- NCBI SRA via `functions.ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`  
- BRC organism search via `functions.search_organisms`  
- BRC assemblies via `functions.get_assemblies`  
- BRC workflows via `functions.get_compatible_workflows`

**Procedures.**  
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)`  
2. `ncbi_find_uids(db="bioproject", accessions="PRJNA1363958")`  
3. `ncbi_linked_records(from_db="bioproject", to_dbs="sra,biosample", ids="1363958")`  
4. `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession="PRJNA1363958", max_results=100)`  
5. `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655", limit=5)`  
6. `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli", limit=5)`  
7. `get_assemblies(taxonomy_id="562")`  
8. `get_compatible_workflows(ploidies=["haploid"], taxonomy_id="562")`

**Statistical Analysis.** Counts were taken directly from returned record fields: GEO `sample_count`, number of `supplementary_files`, SRA run list length, and workflow/assembly counts from the respective result objects. For linked-record outputs containing duplicates, unique counts were inferred by deduplicating repeated UIDs in the returned arrays. Range values for run size and spots were taken from the minimum and maximum across the 6 returned SRA run rows.

## III. Results
**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. GEO and linked raw-data summary for GSE309890**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| GEO accession | GSE309890 |
| Entry type | Series |
| Organism | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| GEO sample count | 6 |
| Supplementary processed files | 1 |
| Supplementary file type | CSV |
| Linked BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Unique linked SRA records | 6 |
| Unique linked BioSample records | 6 |
| Linked PubMed records | 0 |

**Table 2. SRA run characteristics for PRJNA1363958**

| Run | Library strategy | Layout | Platform | Model | Size (MB) | Spots | BioSample |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| SRR36018645 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | ILLUMINA | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 917 | 11,621,726 | SAMN53241894 |
| SRR36018644 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | ILLUMINA | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 801 | 10,415,434 | SAMN53241893 |
| SRR36018643 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | ILLUMINA | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 926 | 11,720,219 | SAMN53241892 |
| SRR36018642 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | ILLUMINA | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 955 | 11,992,461 | SAMN53241891 |
| SRR36018641 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | ILLUMINA | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 948 | 11,997,182 | SAMN53241890 |
| SRR36018640 | RNA-Seq | PAIRED | ILLUMINA | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 894 | 11,363,329 | SAMN53241889 |

**Table 3. Reference and workflow context**

| Resource | Count | Relevant entries |
|---|---:|---|
| Assemblies for *E. coli* taxid 562 | 2 | GCF_000005845.2 (MG1655), GCF_000008865.2 (Sakai) |
| Compatible haploid workflows | 14 | Includes paired-end RNA-seq workflow `rnaseq-pe-main` |

**Findings.**  
The GEO Series has 6 samples and 1 supplementary processed-expression file. The linked BioProject is PRJNA1363958. The BioProject links to 6 unique SRA records and 6 unique BioSample records. All 6 SRA runs are public paired-end RNA-seq runs from Illumina HiSeq 4000. Run sizes range from 801 MB to 955 MB. Spot counts range from 10,415,434 to 11,997,182. A complete genome assembly for the matching MG1655 strain is available as GCF_000005845.2. Retrieved compatible workflows include RNA-seq analysis workflows, including a paired-end RNA-seq workflow.

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The raw reads are available indirectly through SRA, not as raw FASTQ files in the GEO Series record itself. The objective of determining raw-read availability is met: yes, there are 6 linked SRA runs. The assembly part is only partly met: the available reads are RNA-seq transcriptomic reads, so they are not the appropriate input for a standard whole-genome assembly workflow.

**Context.** The GEO record classifies the study as expression profiling by high throughput sequencing and provides only one processed CSV matrix in GEO supplementary files. The SRA metadata confirms that all raw libraries are RNA-Seq, transcriptomic, paired-end Illumina reads. The workflow lookup retrieved RNA-seq processing workflows and did not establish an appropriate de novo genome assembly workflow for these data. The presence of a complete MG1655 reference genome further supports mapping-based RNA-seq analysis rather than assembly.

**Limitations.** GEO metadata does not expose raw reads directly; it only links to the project context. The SRA run listing reported download paths to SRA objects, not FASTQ URLs. The workflow catalog result is limited to workflows indexed in that resource and does not prove that no transcriptome-assembly workflow exists elsewhere. These data do not establish read quality, strand specificity, insert-size suitability, or whether transcriptome assembly for expressed RNAs would be useful for the study aims.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** Yes, GSE309890 has raw reads through SRA under PRJNA1363958. No, these reads are not appropriate for a standard genome assembly of *E. coli* because they are paired-end RNA-seq libraries. The next query worth running is retrieval of per-run metadata in full detail or FASTQ-oriented ENA lookup for the six runs, followed by use of an RNA-seq workflow against the MG1655 reference assembly GCF_000005845.2.

## References
[1] GEO. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890

[2] NCBI E-utilities via `ncbi_find_uids`. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&retmax=10&retstart=0&sort=relevance&retmode=json&db=bioproject&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com

[3] NCBI E-utilities via `ncbi_linked_records`. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/elink.fcgi?dbfrom=bioproject&id=1363958&db=sra%2Cbiosample&retmode=json&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com

[4] NCBI E-utilities via `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project` (esearch). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&retmax=100&retstart=0&sort=relevance&usehistory=y&retmode=json&db=sra&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com

[5] NCBI E-utilities via `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project` (efetch). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?rettype=runinfo&retmode=text&retmax=100&WebEnv=MCID_6aac5c7679a806db150b58e1&query_key=1&retstart=0&db=sra&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
